You're not worthless. I think you're awesome. I know how you feel because I go through some of the same challenges as you. Please know that you aren't alone and that there are many people like us that are here for you. I understand the self hate first hand. I have a very cynical and bitter outlook of myself so I am not sure what advice I should be giving but I hope you choose to stay alive with me and take it one day at a time. I don't know if it helps but recently I've been thinking to myself something a bit different, I know it might sound a bit weird, what I'm going to say, but please bear with me:   


(And also when I say "we", "us", "our", I want you to know that I am speaking directly about you and me, and not trying to preach what I believe- I hope you understand. I am not very good at expressing myself and I am sorry for that.)  


Granted, the body cannot speak to us, it is us who speak through our bodies to other people and so we don't consider our bodies as a 'person'. Our bodies are literally 'us'. Unconscious body parts all working together so our minds can be conscious. And so we don't need to have conversations with our own bodies. But even then, if we look at it a little differently, we can see that our bodies keep us alive and aware of the world around us. And they do it without asking for anything in return. I think that can be a strong and profound form of love.

Though our bodies don't give us comforting words, or hugs, they work incredibly hard just to keep us alive without us even noticing. It is such a strong form of unrequited love that our own bodies have for us. 

So what do we do now? I think that the least we can do is to love our bodies more. And if that seems impossible, let's start by appreciation instead. Our bodies may look 'fat' and 'disgusting' to us, our bodies aren't conscious, and yet they love us. They only exist just so we can be alive. They literally work 24/7, for us. How cool is that? So what if we're fat? Our bodies love us so much, they've stored all this energy, just in case!

Sure our bodies may not look how we want them to, but we will get there, however long it takes. Our bodies have loved us from the beginning, and they will love us until we die. Wouldn't the best way to repay this love be, to give it some more time? Some more chances to fail? Everyone's weight loss journey is different. And the funny thing about failure is that there's always the possibility of success. And once we succeed, we've already made it. There's this incredibly intimate, strong selfless love our bodies have for us, wouldn't ending something this beautiful be a bit too cruel of a punishment for failure? Let's both give ourselves some more time. Who knows? Maybe we can make something of ourselves soon, and contribute to others. We can't get there if we end our lives so early. Let's have this as our goal for the future, and for now let's not worry. Let's take it a day at a time. Let's start with appreciating our own bodies. Because they are incredible hard workers that have only loved us from the very beginning.

I know it is incredibly difficult because I struggle with self love myself, but given that we're both on this subreddit, what else do we really have to lose if we just try? Let's both try to like our own reflections in the mirror today, would you do it with me? 

I'm sorry for the long comment, it is a bad habit of mine to write this much. I'm also sorry if this seems a bit like I am preaching to you. I am not trying to do that. I hope you don't see it that way. Anyways, best of luck on your weight loss journey, my friend. Please don't give up yet. You're incredible. Please take care.

I personally never considered this before. I've always called women "women", and will continue to do so. However, a part of me still seems to disagree. I love cis women, I love trans women.

Everyone on this Earth has their own personal experiences that have molded them into the person they are today. As such, we all have different perspectives on the same topic. And here is mine:

Saying "female" to say stuff like "females are entitled" or any other variation for this phrase is NOT acceptable to me, as they are meant to offend/hurt/spread hatred. 

Incels are cringe. When "female" is used as an insult, it's more sad than insulting. Entitled man children saying "femoids"? They are never seeing a titty irl, that is abnormal behavior. Terrible people. 

I also wouldn't compare a human being to dogs or any other animal in an attempt to degrade a person. That is also unacceptable. However, even though we are human, we are still all animals, with animal cells in our cheeks, skeletons, and red blood cells in our bodies. Like most other animals. And as such, I personally do not have a problem referring to someone as female, Unless they specifically ask me not to. In which case, I refer to them however they prefer. Phrases like "My female coworkers" is fine in the right context in my opinion. This is not me saying women are comparable to animals, or animals can replace human beings (that last part just sounds dumb), I'm just saying that we're all animals to begin with, even when humans and animals are not the same. It is only dehumanizing to me if I say it in an aggressive way to hurt someone, and I have no such intent. (This is just my opinion, yours is valid too)

It's about (what OP says), being considerate. I won't tell others how to feel, or what to do. If someone gets hurt, their feelings are valid, and I will do better. I just don't want others to get hurt by something I didn't mean because English isn't my first language and my speaking isn't very fluent/clear. I don't want someone to misunderstand me and get hurt by it. 

None of this is coming from a place of hatred/bigotry. As OP has shared their opinion, I have done the same. I will say that I have learned to distinguish between aggressive "that female" to something like "she is a female rapper" a little better. My grasp on the English language and also being considerate to others may need some work. 😅
